questions.stem: Dylan asks why debriefing after deception should include a chance to withdraw data.

options.text: Withdrawal is unnecessary if participants seemed unbothered.
options.misconception: relies on apparent lack of distress

options.text: Debriefing alone is enough without withdrawal.
Withdrawal would ruin the dataset and should be avoided.
Participants should control whether their data remain after learning the truth.

questions.explanation: After deception, participants should decide whether their data remain once they know the true purpose.

questions.topic: How minimal risk is determined
questions.learningObjective: Explain why minimal risk needs assessment
questions.stem: In a financial spreadsheet study, 500 records are analysed and no participants are contacted.

options.text: Minimal risk still depends on possible harms from data use.
No contact means the study is automatically minimal risk.
options.misconception: assumes no contact guarantees minimal risk

options.text: Any spreadsheet analysis is high risk.
options.misconception: overstates the risk of spreadsheet analysis

options.text: Risk is zero because the data already exist.

questions.explanation: Even without contact, minimal risk depends on possible harms from how the data are used and reported.

questions.topic: Additional protection owed to a vulnerable group

stimulus.body: A financial spreadsheet study includes 30 participants with cognitive impairments. The study uses existing records and reports only aggregate trends. The researcher plans standard consent procedures for all participants.

options.text: Standard consent is sufficient because the data already exist.
options.misconception: assumes existing data remove consent concerns

options.text: They should be excluded to simplify the study.
options.misconception: excludes participants instead of accommodating them

options.text: Cognitively impaired participants may need capacity assessment and safeguards.
Impairment does not affect consent capacity.

questions.explanation: Participants with cognitive impairments may need capacity assessment and additional safeguards.

questions.topic: Share of replications inside a stated interval

questions.stem: Kylie asks how to use the share of replications inside a stated interval.

options.text: Use it as evidence of consistency with the interval.
Use it as proof that the original hypothesis is true.
Ignore it unless every replication succeeds.
Replace the original result with the replication share.
